verdict.rationale: Kick documents a native per-account reconciliation workflow that compares its transactions against bank or credit card statements and verifies matching amounts and dates, with no missing or duplicate transactions. The docs describe what reconciliation checks, but not a review interface that sorts transactions into matched, unmatched, and duplicate groups, so how deeply it surfaces exceptions is unproven. Missing for 10: documented matched/unmatched/duplicate review views or exception lists, details on how discrepancies are flagged and resolved, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an accountant, I can reconcile each bank account against the ledger with matched, unmatched, and duplicate transactions surfaced for review

citations.quote: Reconciliation verifies that the transactions Kick has on record for an account actually match what the bank has on record - same amounts, same dates, no missing transactions, no duplicates.
Reconciliation is the process of comparing your transactions in Kick against your actual bank or credit card statements to confirm everything is accounted for and accurate.
